review.publication: Local only. No commit, push or deployment.
review.scope: Clothing by use, material and construction; footwear and garment components; remove universal fastener/material claims and false clothing/subtype exclusions.
review.attribution: Reviewed adaptations of Open English WordNet 2025 by the Open English WordNet Team, derived from Princeton WordNet; CC BY 4.0 and Princeton notices remain in docs/quality/2026-10-09-q11.md#sources-and-reuse. Collins and Cambridge independently check garment terminology. Full definitions are not copied; scope decisions and graph mappings are editorial adaptations.
review.context_policy: All new concepts and assertions use U1 with unspecified strength. Clothing purpose, body coverage, material and components are independent classifications. Component presence is not genus membership. Intended protection does not assert certified performance or effectiveness against every hazard.

sense_decisions.scope: Clothing designed as an outer layer for outdoor wear. Do not identify it with every garment that happens to be worn outside.
Clothing designed to be worn beneath outer garments, close to the body. No gender, fabric or specific garment construction is required.
Clothing intended for sports activity. Restrict the dictionary sportswear entry so purely casual fashion is not automatically included.
Clothing intended for manual or physical work. Workwear is not necessarily protective equipment or a uniform.
Clothing intended to protect the wearer or underlying clothing. Broaden the injury-only gloss to include dirt and ordinary weather; no certified protection or hazard coverage is implied.
Clothing designed to resist rain reaching the wearer or underlying clothes. Do not require complete impermeability or a fixed performance rating.
Clothing designed to be worn while sleeping. This is not identical to underwear or to all casual home clothing.
Clothing made by knitting. Do not require wool, a pullover construction, buttons or a particular wearer.
Clothing made using fabric; retain a restricted subject instead of attributing fabric to every clothing article and every footwear design.
Clothing incorporating nylon material. This does not claim pure nylon composition or identify nylon polymer, fiber and woven fabric as one concept.
Clothing having buttons. It may also have other fastening components; do not impose a universal exclusive fastening method.
Clothing having a zipper; the zipper is a component, not a genus of the garment.
Clothing including a garment hood; not every jacket or rain garment has one.
Clothing including sleeves. Do not infer sleeves for every clothing article.
Footwear with a constructed heel component. This is distinct from the anatomical heel and does not require a high heel.
Footwear fitted with laces for fastening; the lace need not be the only fastening mechanism.
An attached or attachable head covering of a garment. Restrict the broader hood meaning; exclude engine cover, exhaust hood, camera accessory and criminal slang.
The neck-area component of a garment; exclude animal collars, shaft collars and necklaces.
The cuff at the wrist end of a sleeve. Broaden folded-back wording to include a sewn or knitted cuff; exclude trouser turn-ups, jewelry, restraints and medical cuffs.
The inner lining component of a garment, distinct from attaching the lining or every generic protective inner surface.
A hook used as a garment fastener. Distinguish it from fishing, hanging and tool hooks.
Clothing including a hook fastener; restrict the old generic hook assertion to this family.
A knitted upper-body garment opening down the front. Do not require buttons, a zipper, wool or a particular collar. Do not place it beneath the narrower Russian sviter record.
A cardigan with buttons, without claiming that every cardigan has them.
A cardigan with a zipper at the front.
A jacket including a hood; this does not by itself imply waterproof construction.
A jacket intended for rain protection. Hood, fastener, material and protection rating are unspecified.
A rain jacket that also has a hood.
A jacket with a zipper; not every jacket is zip-fastened.
A shirt with buttons. Button presence is not imported as universal for the entire shirt family.
A shirt including a collar, with no required collar form or material.
A shirt with cuffs at the ends of its sleeves; not every sleeve must have a cuff.
A jacket with an inner garment lining. No particular fiber, insulation value or waterproof membrane is asserted.
Footwear intended for sporting activity. Do not force every fashion sneaker into this purpose-defined family.
Gloves intended for protection. No specific chemical, impact, thermal or electrical protection is guaranteed.
Headgear intended to resist impact. No safety certification, material or use-specific performance is claimed.
Boots designed for wet-weather use. Rubber is not required of every design.
The rain-boot subset made using rubber. Do not equate every boot, rain boot or waterproof polymer boot with rubber.
The denim textile material, distinct from jeans as clothing. Allow blended fibers; do not assert pure cotton, a fixed weight or every historical manufacturing detail.
Clothing using denim fabric, without requiring every component to have the same material.
A jacket made using denim fabric; material and garment form are distinct classifications.
The English shirt family and Russian rubashka may differ in scope. Defer the T-shirt exclusion rather than blindly importing the dictionary shirt hierarchy.
The dictionary knee-length trouser scope and Russian full-length bruki need review before moving shorts. Only the unambiguous jeans subtype is refined now.
Socks remain distinct from the selected shoe-family footwear record. Do not import the broader dictionary hosiery/footwear hierarchy.
Fashion sneakers and athletic-purpose footwear overlap, but every sneaker is not asserted to be designed for sport.
Wool material, fiber and fabric require a separate textile review. Reject universal wool claims without reclassifying that record here.
The existing shoelace lookup is reused for lace-up footwear. Generic cord, lace and fastening subtypes require separate sense review.
The existing swimsuit is reused later; do not create a duplicate from swimwear or import every broad bathing-clothes synonym.
Vest and waistcoat have regional scope differences. Do not create a duplicate or assume that every vest is underwear.
Anorak, parka and windbreaker should not be imported as a single heavy-jacket sense.
Cardigan the corgi is not the garment.
A vehicle hood is not a garment hood.
An animal collar is not a garment collar.
Handcuffs are not sleeve cuffs.

review.limits: No body/gender restriction, fabric percentage, waterproof rating, protective-equipment certification or care procedure. Keep sports clothing distinct from purely casual fashion, cardigan distinct from the narrower existing Russian sweater record, and denim material distinct from jeans. Shirt/T-shirt, coat/jacket, trouser/shorts, generic cord/shoelace, textile/fiber and remaining footwear distinctions need separate review. No application test suites.

exclusion_review.decision: Reject the false clothing/footwear exclusion while preserving its accepted genus. Reject jeans/trousers exclusion before refining jeans. No other exclusions are changed.

review.collision_decision: No exact normalized cross-language collision is accepted. Existing garments, footwear, fasteners, sleeves, pockets, material records and laundry actions are reused.

refreshed_comparison.caveat: Normalized spelling candidates are not verified identities or missing-concept counts.
